description: We are Stellar Code, a team of four AI students who love hackathons. We're building a project that combines artificial intelligence and agriculture in space environments, using real NASA data. We're strong in programming and machine learning, and we're looking for teammates with experience in agriculture, earth science, or weather, plus a graphic designer and a storyteller to bring our project to life. If you love space and want to learn and create with us, join us!
summary: Earth Mirror is a web prototype that turns NASA Earth data into clear crop rotation options for farmers in Saudi Arabia. Users pick a point on a NASA GIBS satellite map. The tool reads NASA POWER climate data (maximum temperature, rainfall, root-zone wetness) and MODIS NDVI vegetation data for 2020-2025, and combines them in a transparent 0-6 water-stress index that our team designed. Users then type their current crop, and Earth Mirror checks it against local water and heat conditions and compares it with two better-fitting rotations (water-saving and soil-health), showing evidence, data gaps and risks for each. We tested two sample points: Jazan scores 3/6 (moderate) and Qassim 6/6 (high), with 34 of 72 months averaging above 40 °C. This gives farmers an understandable, data-based way to adapt crops to heat and water stress. Soil, market and groundwater data are not yet included.
details:
What it does: Earth Mirror helps a farmer see how heat, rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation changed at a chosen location, and compares crop rotation options. The user clicks a point on a NASA GIBS map (or tries our Jazan and Qassim sample points), views a dashboard with a NASA MODIS NDVI map and timeline, climate indicators and charts, then types the current crop to get three options: the current crop as a baseline, a water-saving rotation, and a soil-health rotation. Each option lists why it is suggested, evidence, benefits, data gaps and risks.

How it works: We retrieve NASA POWER monthly data (T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR, GWETROOT) and MODIS Terra MOD13Q1 v061 NDVI (via NASA AppEEARS). A water-stress index from 0 to 6 adds up to two points each for low rainfall, low root-zone wetness and a high share of months at or above 40 °C. Each crop has a water-need class and a heat-tolerance class, and a simple rule compares them with the local conditions to give a good, fair or poor fit. A topic-limited assistant answers questions about the selected location's data.

Benefits and impact: Farmers get a clear, evidence-based starting point for adapting crops to heat and water stress, with limits stated openly. The method works for any point in Saudi Arabia and can extend to other dry regions.

Tools: Python (requests, pandas, matplotlib), HTML/JavaScript, Leaflet, Chart.js, NASA APIs, a Cloudflare Worker, the Claude API for the assistant, GitHub Pages.

Creative aspect: One transparent index built only from NASA indicators, applied to the crop the user types in, plus a clear display of evidence, gaps and risks.

Factors considered: Jazan and Qassim are sample test points, results are illustrative and not field-validated. NASA POWER and MODIS data are coarse, so small fields are mixed with surrounding land. Crop traits come from general crop knowledge, not NASA data. Index thresholds are our own starting values. Soil, salinity, market and groundwater data are not yet included.
